messages:
leo: kicked off canary -> routing policy: 5% traffic to variant-B (bucket by user.id % 100 < 5). deploying now.

dev-bot: deploy started: canary/variant-B @ 2026-03-20T16:05:07Z :rocket:

sophie: quick FYI — dashboard shows assigned 5% but observed requests for B are ~9%. looks like assignment != observed. cc @aj

aj: on it. can you paste the example user ids where it diverges?

sophie: pasted a small sample in #debug earlier: user ids 1021, 2045, 3050 — all routed to B but their cookies show old session pinned to A.

aj: aha — we use `user.id % 100` for bucket but session sticky cookie is overriding for returning users. new sessions get correct assignment, existing stickies get routed to A. that explains observed > assigned for A actually — but you're seeing B > assigned? odd.

zhang: could be cross-region routing + cookie domain mismatch. some requests hit region-2 which has an older routing config (5% -> 10% historically) and sticky cookie persists. ops, any recent config rollbacks in region-2?

ops: region-2 had a hotfix 03/18 that touched routing config but it was rolled forward. gist: no explicit rollback since then. I'll grep the config history.

maria: before we dig deeper, we should check SRM/sample-ratio test. quick SQL I use:

```
SELECT variant, COUNT(*) as observed, SUM(assigned_flag) as assigned_count
FROM events
WHERE experiment_id = 'canary-2026-03-20-variantB'
GROUP BY variant;
```

then compute chi2 p-value.

aj: ran that against prod-recent window (16:00-16:20). results: A observed=18230 assigned=18000; B observed=1790 assigned=4500.

maria: that's a huge mismatch — SRM p < 1e-6. assignment << observed for B? wait numbers look flipped — are you sure `assigned_flag` semantics are correct?

aj: good catch — assigned_flag was 1 for A earlier. I re-ran with explicit assigned_variant field. new numbers: A observed=18000 assigned=18230; B observed=4500 assigned=1790. so B observed > assigned by ~2500.

sophie: confirms what dashboard showed. so more live traffic hitting B than the assignment suggests, meaning something is over-routing to B.

lee (ops): (edited) checked region configs. region-2 still had staged rule from 03/15 that used percentage 10 for B and a slightly different hashing key `session.id` — it was supposed to be removed but not propagated. ops will sync now.

aj: until configs sync, we should pause ramp. question for the rollout guard: do we have an SRM threshold or assignment deviation guard that auto-holds? I don't think console enforces sample-ratio checks today.

maria: we have end-criteria code: min_samples=5k per variant and delta CI stable for 30m, but no SRM guard. we need both: (1) hold if |observed_assigned_ratio - 1| > 0.03 for either variant AND (2) min_samples. otherwise stats are invalid.

product-bot: note created: RB-3421 "add sample-ratio guard for rollouts" assigned to eng-platform.

aj: for immediate action: I'm in favor of pausing the canary traffic increase and reverting routing config to previous global policy. can we flip to 0.5% and let sessions drain?

leo: +1. i'd rather stable small sample than noisy skew. also we must communicate to product owners.

sophie: I'll post an update on the customer-facing incident ticker: "Canary pause for routing config mismatch; no customer impact expected."

aj: quick command to reduce canary via API:

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  https://console.redwood/api/rollouts/adjust
  -d '{"experiment":"canary-2026-03-20-variantB","target_pct":0.5}'
```

ops: executed. routing % set to 0.5. waiting for propagation (TTL ~30s).

dev-bot: canary update: variant-B traffic -> 0.5% (applied 2026-03-20T16:08:42Z)

maria: follow-ups we need:
- add SRM check to rollout guard (threshold 0.03) as a hard hold
- add per-region routing config diffing and a console view for assigned vs observed counts
- add telemetry alert when observed/assigned ratio deviates >2% for 5m
- backfill experiment metric to validate whether the skew biased metric estimates

aj: I'll file tasks and take ownership of the SRM guard PR. reference: quick chi2 code in py:

```
from scipy.stats import chisquare
chisquare(f_obs=[obs_A, obs_B], f_exp=[exp_A, exp_B])
```

zhang: I'll make a small console patch: show assigned vs observed histogram under experiment details and highlight drift.

ops: synced configs in region-2. confirmed old staged rule removed. re-checking live counts.

aj: recomputed after sync (16:14): A observed=18400 assigned=18450; B observed=900 assigned=920. much closer. SRM p=0.38 now.

sophie: looks good. can we resume planned ramp once sessions age out? probably safe to ramp to 2% in 1 hour.

leo: decision: pause ramp (done), fix infra config (done), add SRM & telemetry (owners assigned), resume to 2% in 1h if observed/assigned stays within 2% for 10m. created follow-up ENG-1234.

product-bot: note updated: RB-3421 linked to ENG-1234, target milestone: next sprint.

maria: thanks everyone. lesson: we need proactive per-region diff checks and console guard for SRM. I'll draft a short retro for release notes.

leo: thanks. closing thread — unless anyone objects to the action items.

sophie: no objections. :thumbsup:

ops: closing the loop on the config push, will watch for 30m.

dev-bot: thread archived by automation (rolled-up as incident-free pause).
